qt: to the Commission Aldo Patriciello (PPE) Subject:

On 27 September 2021, in his answer to question E-003783/20211, Commissioner Nicolas Schmit described the activity in question as ‘ancillary’, stating that he did not consider it appropriate to address the category of tax judges as such in separate infringement proceedings against Italy. On 29 November 2021, in his answer to question E-004491/20212,Commissioner Schmit also stated that the Commission was not able to undertake a full legal analysis of the compliance with EU law of the national regulatory regime applying to tax judges. Given the further developments in this matter (see complaint No CPLT(2023)02181) and subsequent requests for information between the parties, will the Commission initiate a prompt review of the request that the rights of Italy’s tax judges be recognised in the light of EU legislation and current case-law, as consolidated in relation to cases – of less consequence, moreover – involving honorary judges in Italy?
at: (English version) to the Commission Aldo Patriciello (PPE) (18 January 2024) Subject: Situation of tax judges in Italy On 27 September 2021, in his answer to Question E-003783/2021 (1), Commissioner Nicolas Schmit described the activity in question as ‘ancillary’, stating that he did not consider it appropriate to address the category of tax judges as such in separate infringement proceedings against Italy. On 29 November 2021, in his answer to Question E-004491/2021 (2),Commissioner Schmit also stated that the Commission was not able to undertake a full legal analysis of the compliance with EU law of the national regulatory regime applying to tax judges. Given the further developments in this matter (see complaint No CPLT(2023)02181) and subsequent requests for information between the parties, will the Commission initiate a prompt review of the request that the rights of Italy’s tax judges be recognised in the light of EU legislation and current case-law, as consolidated in relation to cases — of less consequence, moreover — involving honorary judges in Italy? (7 March 2024) The Commission recently received several complaints of lay tax judges about the national rules on the Italian tax judiciary, as reformed in 2022 (by Law No 130/2022, amending Legislative Decree 545/1992 (3)). The complainants raise issues of discrimination in respect of working conditions including remuneration, annual leave, and social security protection. In light of these recent complaints and additional information supplied by the complainants, the Commission services are currently assessing the conformity of the reformed national legislation with EU law requirements. The new information is notably taken into account to ascertain the worker status of lay tax judges (‘giudici tributari’) for the purposes of the EU labour law acquis. The Commission services specifically assess compliance with the principle of non-discrimination of part-time workers vis-à-vis comparable full-time workers, considering the differences in treatment between lay tax judges and tax magistrates (‘professional tax judges’) under the reformed national rules.
